content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with a [product_name] and [product_name] operator device. After running my machine for a few days, the display stopped working, but I could still connect using [product_name] software and IP 192.168.1.42 through my router. When I tried to update the program again (after many successful attempts before), the computer couldn't connect to 192.168.1.42. I also tried pinging this IP and lost some packets, but received responses from 169.254.13.216. So I set my laptop's IP to 169.254.13.216 and was able to ping the device successfully. It seems the device's IP changed on its own. However, even though I get ping responses, I cannot connect via [product_name] software. Why? When I set my PC's IP to 169.254.13.216, I can't set netmask 255.255.255.0— the PC always switches it to 255.255.0.0. I tried changing it on the device but still couldn't connect via [product_name] software. There are no warnings during download attempts. How do I reestablish connection and update my program? Is it possible to change the IP on this device without a functioning display, for example, using the [product_name] operator device? Can I update the device using an SD card even if the display isn’t working? The device didn’t have the default IP when I first powered it. I would appreciate quick help— I need to fix issues in my program as soon as possible. Thanks, [user_name]

Hello, The [product_name] device does not modify its own IP address automatically. Is there a program stored on an SD card plugged in? If so, try changing the IP address set in the program stored on the SD card. You can change the IP address: - Using the [product_name] operator device - Using an SD card with a program specifying a different IP. Just power on the [product_name] and it will read the program. Your problem seems related to network settings: - Check the IP information from the device via the operator panel - Directly connect your PC to the device and attempt connection The subnet mask should match your IP address and its class. Hope this helps.

I haven't changed the IP address; downloading and online simulation worked previously, but now I can't connect. I suspect the [product_name] device might be damaged, as the display is also not functioning. Previously, I could edit IP settings in the device's menu when the display worked— shouldn't those same settings be present in the operator panel’s menu? Did I understand correctly that I should save my program as LOGO_U_P.bin on an SD card, insert it into the device, and then power up so it updates the program? Will the operator device show this process? Thanks, [user_name]

I've tried updating the program via SD card, but it doesn't seem to read it and I can't find further info in the manual. I also checked the network settings through the operator device again, but there aren't any network options accessible. Can you explain, step by step, how to change both program and IP address using the SD card? My PC won't accept netmask 255.255.255.0 for IP 169.254.13.216—it always changes it to 255.255.0.0. Is there a workaround? I'd prefer not to buy another [product_name] device to fix this issue. Regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], The documentation for the relevant application (see page 9 and 10) has images guiding you on how to set an IP address in the device menu. These same menu options should be available on the operator panel. You can review it here: [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter connectivity loss when the device display fails, making it difficult to update programs and network configurations. Although the device still runs its automated tasks, users cannot update or restore connections as before, resulting in confusion. Accessing network settings via the operator panel proves inconsistent, and updating the system via SD card lacks clarity and clear procedural documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate straightforward methods for restoring network connectivity and updating the device’s software when the main display is not working, ideally using the operator panel or an SD card, guided by clear and comprehensive instructions.
